newsitem.title: FRANCE: Europe ad spending to rise 4.9 pct in 1997 - Havas.
newsitem.headline: Europe ad spending to rise 4.9 pct in 1997 - Havas.

text.p: Spending on advertising in western Europe is likely to rise by 4.9 percent in 1997 compared with 1996, according to the annual Europub review published by French communications group Havas on Tuesday.

The review, of 1996 advertising spending in Europe's eight largest markets, chronicled on-line multi-media spending for the first time and said the outlays in this high-profile field were still very modest.

"With no clear signs of economic growth shaping up in 1997, Europub expects advertising markets to be affected once again and estimates the full-year rise at 4.9 percent," a Havas statement on the review said.
In 1996 total advertising outlays came to $130 billion, a 4.6 percent rise on 1995, it said.
Direct marketing and outdoor advertising were the fastest-growing sectors, rising seven percent and six percent respectively, it said.
Germany remained the largest national market by far, with a steady 29.3 percent of total spending, but the strongest growth came in Britain with a rise of 7.3 percent in spending.

Multimedia outlays accounted for $7.5 million in Germany, $2.8 million in the Netherlands and $1 million in France, all of which are very low compared with multimedia spending of $300 million in the United States last year, the statement said.
"In 1997, on-line advertising expenditure is expected to climb steeply in Europe, although compared with above-the-line spending it should remain negligible for some time to come," it said.

Europub quantifies and analyses advertising expenditure on above-the-line, below-the-line and multimedia vehicles in Germany, Britain, France, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands, Belgium and Switzerland, which together represent 80 percent of total spending in western Europe.
